text.p: Zimbabwe's Agriculture Minister Denis Norman resigned on Monday, becoming the first cabinet minister to voluntarily leave President Robert Mugabe's government in the last 17 years.
Norman, 66, told a news conference that he was leaving active politics to concentrate on his private farming business and to make way for a younger person.
Norman was one of only two whites in Mugabe's 25-member cabinet and has been a minister for most of the last 17 years.

He was first appointed agriculture minister at Zimbabwe's independence in 1980, and served as transport and energy minister in the early 1990s. He became agriculture minister again in May 1995, a key post in the agriculture-based southern African state.
Norman denied suggestions he was resigning over policy differences with Mugabe or other cabinet colleagues.
The government last year introduced a controversial 10 percent tobacco levy on growers and merchants, and is considering a comprehensive farming levy, yet to be detailed.
Industry analysts have suggested that Norman was uncomfortable with these taxes, but he has denied this.
"The decision to leave is entirely my own, and has not been brought about by any lack of faith in the government, disillusionment, pressure, stress or deteriorating health," Norman said.
